metadata.cypher_query:
MATCH (e:Employee)
WHERE e.department IS NOT NULL AND e.hourly_rate IS NOT NULL
WITH e.department AS department, AVG(e.hourly_rate) AS avg_hourly_rate
ORDER BY avg_hourly_rate DESC
WITH COLLECT({department: department, avg_hourly_rate: avg_hourly_rate}) AS rows
UNWIND rows AS row
WITH row, rows[0] AS top_row
RETURN row.department AS department,
       row.avg_hourly_rate AS avg_hourly_rate,
       CASE WHEN row.department = top_row.department THEN true ELSE false END AS is_highest_department,
       top_row.department AS highest_department,
       top_row.avg_hourly_rate AS highest_avg_hourly_rate
ORDER BY avg_hourly_rate DESC

MATCH (e:Employee)-[:HAS_POSITION]->(pos:Position)
WITH e, pos,
     CASE
       WHEN e.years_experience IS NULL OR pos.min_years IS NULL OR pos.max_years IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
       WHEN e.years_experience >= pos.min_years AND e.years_experience <= pos.max_years THEN 'matched'
       ELSE 'mismatched'
     END AS fit_status
WITH fit_status,
     COUNT(*) AS employee_count,
     COLLECT({employee: e.name, years_experience: e.years_experience, position: pos.name, level: pos.level, min_years: pos.min_years, max_years: pos.max_years}) AS employees
RETURN fit_status, employee_count, employees
ORDER BY CASE fit_status WHEN 'matched' THEN 1 WHEN 'mismatched' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

MATCH (e:Employee)
WHERE e.hire_date IS NOT NULL
WITH date(e.hire_date).year AS hire_year, COUNT(e) AS new_hire_count
RETURN hire_year, new_hire_count
ORDER BY hire_year ASC

MATCH (e:Employee)-[:WORKS_ON]->(p:Project)
WITH e, COUNT(DISTINCT p) AS actual_project_count
WHERE actual_project_count > e.max_projects
RETURN e.name AS employee, e.max_projects AS max_projects, actual_project_count
ORDER BY actual_project_count DESC, employee ASC
LIMIT 200

MATCH (e:Employee)-[:HAS_SKILL]->(s:Skill)
WITH s.name AS skill, COUNT(DISTINCT e) AS employee_count
RETURN skill, employee_count
ORDER BY employee_count DESC, skill ASC
LIMIT 10

MATCH (s:Skill)
WHERE s.market_demand = $marketDemand
OPTIONAL MATCH (e:Employee)-[r:HAS_SKILL]->(s)
WITH s, COUNT(DISTINCT e) AS employee_count
RETURN s.name AS skill, employee_count, s.market_demand AS market_demand, s.category AS category, s.difficulty AS difficulty
ORDER BY employee_count ASC, skill ASC
LIMIT 1

MATCH (e:Employee)-[r:HAS_SKILL]->(s:Skill)
WHERE r.proficiency = $proficiency
  AND ANY(skillName IN $skillNames WHERE toLower(s.name) = toLower(skillName))
WITH e.department AS department, COUNT(DISTINCT e) AS employee_count, COLLECT(DISTINCT e.name) AS employees
RETURN department, employee_count, employees
ORDER BY employee_count DESC, department ASC
LIMIT 200

MATCH (e:Employee)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e)-[r:HAS_SKILL]->(s:Skill)
WITH e.job_type AS job_type,
     COUNT(s) AS skill_count_per_employee,
     AVG(r.effective_rate) AS avg_effective_rate_per_employee
RETURN job_type,
       AVG(skill_count_per_employee) AS avg_skill_count,
       AVG(avg_effective_rate_per_employee) AS avg_effective_rate
ORDER BY job_type

MATCH (p:Project)
WHERE p.budget_allocated IS NOT NULL AND p.budget_allocated <> 0 AND p.budget_spent IS NOT NULL
WITH p.status AS status,
     SUM(p.budget_spent) AS total_budget_spent,
     SUM(p.budget_allocated) AS total_budget_allocated,
     CASE WHEN SUM(p.budget_allocated) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE toFloat(SUM(p.budget_spent)) / SUM(p.budget_allocated) END AS execution_rate
RETURN status, total_budget_spent, total_budget_allocated, execution_rate
ORDER BY status

MATCH (p:Project)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)<-[w:WORKS_ON]-(e:Employee)
WITH p, COUNT(DISTINCT e) AS actual_assigned
WHERE actual_assigned < p.required_headcount
RETURN p.name AS project, p.required_headcount AS required_headcount, actual_assigned AS actual_assigned, (p.required_headcount - actual_assigned) AS shortage, p.status AS status, p.start_date AS start_date
ORDER BY shortage DESC, project ASC
LIMIT 200

RETURN employee, certificate_count, active_project_count
ORDER BY certificate_count DESC, active_project_count DESC, employee ASC

metadata.cypher_query:
MATCH (mentor:Employee)-[:MENTORS]->(mentee:Employee)
WITH mentor, COUNT(mentee) AS mentee_count
WITH COLLECT({mentor: mentor, mentee_count: mentee_count}) AS mentor_stats,
     AVG(toFloat(mentee_count)) AS avg_mentees_per_mentor
UNWIND mentor_stats AS stat
WITH stat, avg_mentees_per_mentor
WITH avg_mentees_per_mentor,
     stat.mentor.department AS department,
     stat.mentor.id AS mentor_id,
     stat.mentor.name AS mentor_name,
     COALESCE(pos.name, 'Unknown') AS position_name,
     COALESCE(pos.level, 'Unknown') AS position_level,
     stat.mentee_count AS mentee_count
OPTIONAL MATCH (stat.mentor)-[:HAS_POSITION]->(pos:Position)
WITH avg_mentees_per_mentor, department, position_name, position_level, mentor_id, mentor_name, mentee_count
RETURN avg_mentees_per_mentor,
       department,
       position_name,
       position_level,
       COUNT(DISTINCT mentor_id) AS mentor_count,
       AVG(toFloat(mentee_count)) AS avg_mentees_in_group,
       COLLECT(DISTINCT mentor_name)[0..20] AS example_mentors
ORDER BY mentor_count DESC, avg_mentees_in_group DESC
LIMIT 200

MATCH (e:Employee)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(p:Project)
WITH e.name AS employee, p.name AS project,
     w.allocated_hours AS allocated_hours,
     w.actual_hours AS actual_hours,
     (coalesce(w.actual_hours, 0) - coalesce(w.allocated_hours, 0)) AS hours_gap,
     abs(coalesce(w.actual_hours, 0) - coalesce(w.allocated_hours, 0)) AS abs_hours_gap
RETURN employee, project, allocated_hours, actual_hours, hours_gap
ORDER BY abs_hours_gap DESC, employee ASC, project ASC
LIMIT 200

MATCH (d:Department)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Project)-[:OWNED_BY]->(d)
WITH d, COALESCE(SUM(p.budget_million), 0) AS total_project_budget_million
RETURN d.name AS department,
       d.budget_billion AS department_budget_billion,
       total_project_budget_million,
       CASE
         WHEN d.budget_billion IS NULL OR d.budget_billion = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE toFloat(total_project_budget_million) / (d.budget_billion * 1000.0)
       END AS budget_ratio
ORDER BY budget_ratio DESC, department

MATCH (d:Department)-[:LOCATED_AT]->(o:Office)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e:Employee)-[:BELONGS_TO]->(d)
WITH o, d, COUNT(e) AS department_headcount
RETURN o.name AS office, COUNT(DISTINCT d) AS department_count, SUM(department_headcount) AS total_employees, SUM(d.budget_billion) AS total_department_budget_billion
ORDER BY office

MATCH (p:Project)
WHERE p.type = $projectType AND p.status = $projectStatus
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)<-[w:WORKS_ON]-(e:Employee)
WITH p, p.required_headcount AS required_headcount, COUNT(DISTINCT e) AS current_assigned
RETURN p.name AS project_name,
       required_headcount,
       current_assigned,
       (current_assigned - required_headcount) AS headcount_gap,
       CASE
         WHEN current_assigned < required_headcount THEN '부족'
         WHEN current_assigned = required_headcount THEN '충족'
         ELSE '초과'
       END AS staffing_status
ORDER BY headcount_gap ASC, project_name ASC
LIMIT 200

violations.claim: LangChain 요구: 어떤 행에서는 고급 2명 필수
violations.reason: 제시된 graph_results 샘플에는 LangChain에 대해 required_proficiency=고급, required_headcount=2 인 REQUIRES 행이 없습니다. 샘플상 LangChain은 중급 우대(행 10, 18, 29, 43) 또는 고급 필수 2명(행 2, 22)로 보이지만, 행 2와 22의 LangChain 보유자는 각각 초급/중급이라 '요구' 자체가 고급 2명 필수라고 단정한 근거는 샘플에 없습니다.

violations.claim: available/partial 인원 예시: 임지환(partial, Scikit-learn·Python·PyTorch 고급)
violations.reason: 샘플에는 임지환이 추천시스템 고도화에 WORKS_ON 중이며 Scikit-learn/Python/PyTorch 모두 고급인 것은 맞지만, availability=partial인 임지환은 제시된 샘플 행들에서 p.required_headcount=3, duration_months=6 버전의 프로젝트와 연결됩니다. 응답은 이를 현재 전체 커버 판단의 가용 인원 예시로 일반화했는데, 프로젝트 버전/행 차이를 구분하지 않아 대상-값 재조합 소지가 있습니다.

metadata.cypher_query:
MATCH (p:Project)-[req:REQUIRES]->(s:Skill)
WHERE toLower(p.name) = toLower($projectName)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)<-[w:WORKS_ON]-(e:Employee)-[hs:HAS_SKILL]->(s)
WITH p, req, s, w, e, hs,
     CASE req.required_proficiency
       WHEN '초급' THEN 1
       WHEN '중급' THEN 2
       WHEN '고급' THEN 3
       ELSE 0
     END AS requiredLevel,
     CASE hs.proficiency
       WHEN '초급' THEN 1
       WHEN '중급' THEN 2
       WHEN '고급' THEN 3
       WHEN '전문가' THEN 4
       ELSE 0
     END AS employeeLevel
RETURN p, req, s, w, e, hs
LIMIT 200

MATCH (p:Project)
WHERE toLower(p.name) = toLower($projectName)
MATCH (e:Employee)
WHERE e.availability <> 'unavailable'
  AND NOT EXISTS { MATCH (e)-[:WORKS_ON]->(p) }
OPTIONAL MATCH (e)-[r1:HAS_SKILL]->(s1:Skill)
WHERE toLower(s1.name) = toLower($skill1)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e)-[r2:HAS_SKILL]->(s2:Skill)
WHERE toLower(s2.name) = toLower($skill2)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e)-[r3:HAS_SKILL]->(s3:Skill)
WHERE toLower(s3.name) = toLower($skill3)
WITH p, e, r1, s1, r2, s2, r3, s3,
     ((CASE WHEN s1 IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +
      (CASE WHEN s2 IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) +
      (CASE WHEN s3 IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS matchedSkillCount
WHERE matchedSkillCount > 0
RETURN p, e, r1, s1, r2, s2, r3, s3
LIMIT 200

violations.claim: "Python은 필수 수준 이상이고 단가도 허용 범위 이내라 우선 추천 가능합니다." (조시윤 관련)
violations.reason: graph_results에서 Python의 required_proficiency는 고급이고, 조시윤의 Python proficiency는 전문가로 확인되지만, 응답의 '필수 수준 이상' 판단은 Scikit-learn/LangChain/PyTorch 등 다른 필수 스킬 충족 여부를 확인하지 않은 채 추천 적합성을 단정합니다. 샘플 근거만으로는 전체 필수 스킬 기준 충족 추천으로 단정하기 어렵습니다.

violations.claim: "단가 경쟁력이 좋고 Python 커버가 가능합니다." (우민서 관련 추천 맥락)
violations.reason: 우민서는 Python 전문가, Scikit-learn 중급은 확인되지만 전체 필수 스킬 기준 추천 가능 인원으로 제시하려면 다른 필수 스킬 충족 여부가 필요합니다. graph_results에는 우민서의 LangChain/PyTorch 충족 정보가 없습니다.

violations.claim: "Scikit-learn 필수 스킬 충족 측면에서 유효한 후보입니다." (황승민 관련)
violations.reason: 황승민의 Scikit-learn 고급은 확인되지만, 질문은 추천시스템 고도화의 필수 스킬 기준으로 후보 추천을 요구합니다. graph_results상 다른 필수 스킬(Python/LangChain/PyTorch) 충족 여부 없이 전체 후보로 유효하다고 단정한 것은 근거 부족입니다.

violations.claim: "PyTorch 필수 스킬 대응 후보로 매우 적합합니다." (최준서 관련)
violations.reason: 최준서의 PyTorch 전문가와 단가 조건은 확인되지만, 다른 필수 스킬 충족 여부는 graph_results에 없습니다. 전체 필수 스킬 기준의 추천 적합성을 단정한 표현은 샘플 근거를 넘습니다.

MATCH (p:Project)-[req:REQUIRES]->(s:Skill)

  AND req.importance = '필수'

WITH p, req, s, e, hs
ORDER BY req.priority ASC, hs.years_used DESC, hs.proficiency DESC

MATCH (e:Employee)-[r:HAS_SKILL]->(s:Skill)
WHERE e.department = $department
  AND NOT ANY(excludedSkill IN $excludedSkills WHERE toLower(s.name) = toLower(excludedSkill))
RETURN e, r, s
LIMIT 200

MATCH (e:Employee)-[:HAS_CERTIFICATE]->(c:Certificate)
WHERE toLower(c.name) <> toLower($certificateName)
WITH e.name AS employee, COLLECT(DISTINCT c.name) AS certificates, COUNT(DISTINCT c) AS certificate_count
RETURN employee, certificates, certificate_count
ORDER BY employee ASC
LIMIT 200
